scope: Formal Cosmos3 wrist-only SFT dataset-lineage start gate
summary: Formal wrist-only SFT now fails closed unless a WORKING all-record pixel audit binds the exact selected dataset contract; smoke remains explicitly non-quality-bearing.
evidence: The formal controller requires --dataset-lineage-audit for condition-mode=wrist_only.
The validator requires the audit method, WORKING status, accepted=true, exact dataset-contract SHA-256, exact record count, and accepted=true on every record.
Training metadata stores the audit path, audit hash, aggregate extrema, record count, and bound dataset-contract hash.
The recorded training method now distinguishes wrist_only from anchor_multiview rather than using one ambiguous method name.
All 62 Cosmos3-focused CPU tests pass in 0.71 seconds; targeted Ruff, py_compile, and whitespace checks pass.
lessons: A strict audit is only useful if the formal training launcher requires and cryptographically binds it.
A memory/backpropagation smoke can validate infrastructure but must not bypass data-lineage or quality gates for formal training.
limitations: No remote all-record audit or formal optimization has run because current SSH access is sandbox-blocked and eight sufficiently free GPUs have not been observed.
This gate does not itself improve generated visual quality; it prevents invalid supervision from being used or mislabeled.
next_actions: Run the remote all-record audit after data materialization and pass its immutable result to the unchanged formal launcher.
After formal training, generate all four validation samples, select no checkpoint unless every strict identity/view/motion gate passes, and build a labeled demo only from an accepted result.
